subtitle: Lesson 46 · Scaling Up: Mixed Precision & Multi-GPU Basics

eyebrow: Wrap the forward pass, not the model
code:
with torch.autocast(device_type="cuda",
                    dtype=torch.float16):
    output = model(inputs)
    loss = loss_fn(output, targets)

loss.backward()

# matmuls/convs run in FP16
# softmax, loss stay in FP32
caption: autocast triages which ops are safe in reduced precision.

steps.label: GradScaler fixes it
steps.sub: scales the loss up before backward, down before step()

code:
scaler = torch.amp.GradScaler("cuda")

for x, y in train_loader:
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.float16):
        out = model(x)
        loss = loss_fn(out, y)
    scaler.scale(loss).backward()
    scaler.step(optimizer)
    scaler.update()
caption: scale -> backward -> step -> update, every iteration.

eyebrow: BF16: usually no scaler at all
code:
for x, y in train_loader:
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    with torch.autocast("cuda",
                        dtype=torch.bfloat16):
        out = model(x)
        loss = loss_fn(out, y)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
caption: BF16's wider range rarely underflows -- no GradScaler needed.
